players.product: OlympusMAX dry / adiabatic coolers and Marley Everest cooling towers for data-center heat rejection

quarterly_data.signal: SPX's HVAC reportable segment (package and process cooling products and engineered air movement for industrial markets including data center and power generation, plus heating products) had revenues of $1,518.2 in 2025 versus $1,364.7 in 2024 and $1,122.3 in 2023 (in millions), and backlog of $584.5 as of December 31, 2025 versus $436.8 a year earlier, including $51.3 from the Sigma & Omega acquisition; approximately 83% of that backlog is expected to be recognized as revenue during 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: HVAC revenue $1,518.2 million in 2025 (vs $1,364.7 million); HVAC backlog $584.5 million at Dec 31, 2025 (vs $436.8 million), ~83% to revenue in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 capital expenditures were $92.1 (in millions), including $62.0 related to capacity expansions for the engineered air movement and handling and cooling products businesses within the HVAC segment (HVAC segment capex $82.9 versus $31.9 in 2024). In the fourth quarter of 2025 SPX entered into an agreement to purchase land and buildings for a new facility, to be enhanced with further machinery and equipment in 2026 to increase capacity for those businesses. Contract liabilities increased significantly due to larger down payments received at the cooling products and air handling businesses to support higher backlog executing in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $92.1 million incl. $62.0 million for cooling / air-movement capacity expansion; HVAC segment capex $82.9 million (vs $31.9 million)
